record_contract.record_layout: torch int64 pair (timestamp, (aux << 32) | tag) serialized as 16-byte FILITE02 records
record_contract.clock: CuTeDSL %globaltimer nanoseconds; explicit timer_hz=1e9 in dump meta

conventions.compiler: CuTeDSL/CUTLASS targeting sm_90 or the explicit B300 architecture sm_100a/sm_103a
conventions.collector: nsys plus GPU metrics; dump raw CuTeDSL records before Perfetto conversion
conventions.event_ids: Use event_id and event_id_const exactly as declared in knowledge/semantic_ids.json; never 0 and never assign a language-local sequence.
conventions.levels: Measure off, entry-only, and full builds so instrumentation overhead is separable.
conventions.scope_selection: Use grid_sync and operator boundaries to choose task versus phase; source keywords alone do not decide record_scope.
conventions.name_policy: display_name and trace name are the semantic_id; aliases are match-only and never rendered.
conventions.evidence_policy: This file is a reference library. Only a target-card hard run can raise evidence_status to measured.
conventions.safety: Pack each 64-bit record field as (aux << 32) | tag so the lower 32 bits stay the tag and no unsigned wrap changes event ids. Check slot < n_slots and count < cap before every write, mask the tag to 0x0FFF, flag lane-full and slot-out-of-range overflow, and fail delivery on overflow. Dump meta must explicitly include arch, backend, gran=warp|cta, card, and timer_hz=1e9; never infer AMD from timer_hz alone.

import os
from cutlass import Float16, Float32, Int32, Int64, cute
from fi_cute import fi_open, fi_b, fi_e, fi_close

EV_GEMM = Int32(10)
ARCH = os.environ["WEAVEPROFILER_ARCH"]  # sm_90, sm_100a, or sm_103a
BACKEND = "cutedsl_nv"
GRAN = 0  # 0=warp lane 0; 1=linear CTA thread 0
META = {"arch": ARCH, "backend": BACKEND, "gran": "warp" if GRAN == 0 else "cta"}

@cute.jit
def pack_record(tag: Int32, aux: Int32) -> Int64:
    return (Int64(aux) << 32) | (Int64(tag) & Int64(0xFFFFFFFF))

@cute.jit
def gemm_segment(records, overflow, mma_atom, accumulator, tensor_a, tensor_b, gmem_c, store_atom):
    ctx = fi_open(records, overflow, EV_GEMM, Int32(8), fi_level=2, fi_gran=GRAN)
    aux = Int32(0)
    ctx = fi_b(ctx, EV_GEMM, aux)
    cute.gemm(mma_atom, accumulator, tensor_a, tensor_b, accumulator)
    ctx = fi_e(ctx, EV_GEMM, aux)
    cute.copy(store_atom, accumulator, gmem_c)
    ctx = fi_close(ctx)
    return ctx, pack_record(EV_GEMM, aux), META

event_boundaries.begin: Immediately before the first A/B tile load for the selected GEMM segment.
event_boundaries.end: After the final accumulator update and asynchronous MMA completion wait; close the operator task after the final C write.

patterns.record_scope: task when the whole grid_sync-separated segment is GEMM; phase only when nested inside a larger operator.
patterns.writer_rule: CuTeDSL uses value-style recording: every fi_open/fi_b/fi_e/fi_m/fi_close call returns an updated context and the caller must assign it. With FI_GRAN=0 only lane 0 of each physical warp writes. With FI_GRAN=1 only the CTA linear thread 0 writes; for a multidimensional block compute tx + BLOCK_X * (ty + BLOCK_Y * tz) and pass that predicate to fi_open_by. Checking only threadIdx.x is invalid.
patterns.buffer_rule: Pack each 64-bit record field as (aux << 32) | tag so the lower 32 bits stay the tag and no unsigned wrap changes event ids. Check slot < n_slots and count < cap before every write, mask the tag to 0x0FFF, flag lane-full and slot-out-of-range overflow, and fail delivery on overflow. Dump meta must explicitly include arch, backend, gran=warp|cta, card, and timer_hz=1e9; never infer AMD from timer_hz alone.
language_notes: CuTeDSL is value-style: fi_b/fi_e return a new FiCtx and dropping the returned context silently loses records; device helpers lower via LLVM IR atomicrmw add + @llvm.nvvm.read.ptx.sreg.globaltimer with cute.arch.barrier() brackets around cute.gemm (measured on B300 sm_103a at 85.20 TFLOPS / 403.41 us, 526,336 spans, 200 kHz cold-HBM [Throughput %] curves at pid=1 / upid=1).
Record storage packs tag and aux as (aux << 32) | tag; the decoder must split the low tag and high aux fields before pairing events.
Set arch/backend/gran explicitly in dump meta: H20 uses sm_90, while B300 must be sm_100a or sm_103a and may not be collapsed to one architecture.
FI_GRAN=0 records one lane per warp; FI_GRAN=1 records one CTA. Use linear thread id for CTA scope and never assume a 1-D block when threadIdx.x == 0 is used as the predicate.
validation: Compare every C element for all M, N, K shapes against a reference implementation.
Check C shape, dtype, element count, and NaN/Inf policy.
Require a gemm task and nested mma spans to stay inside it.
Cover tails and non-multiple tiles.

import os
from cutlass import Float16, Float32, Int32, Int64, cute
from fi_cute import fi_open, fi_b, fi_e, fi_close

EV_ATTENTION = Int32(11)
ARCH = os.environ["WEAVEPROFILER_ARCH"]  # sm_90, sm_100a, or sm_103a
BACKEND = "cutedsl_nv"
GRAN = 0  # 0=warp lane 0; 1=linear CTA thread 0
META = {"arch": ARCH, "backend": BACKEND, "gran": "warp" if GRAN == 0 else "cta"}

@cute.jit
def pack_record(tag: Int32, aux: Int32) -> Int64:
    return (Int64(aux) << 32) | (Int64(tag) & Int64(0xFFFFFFFF))

@cute.jit
def attention_segment(records, overflow, qk_atom, pv_atom, q, k, v, scores, out, gmem_out, store_atom):
    ctx = fi_open(records, overflow, EV_ATTENTION, Int32(8), fi_level=2, fi_gran=GRAN)
    aux = Int32(0)
    ctx = fi_b(ctx, EV_ATTENTION, aux)
    cute.gemm(qk_atom, scores, q, k, scores)
    scores = cute.math.exp2(scores - scores.reduce(cute.ReductionOp.MAX, -Float32.inf, 0), fastmath=True)
    scores = scores * cute.arch.rcp_approx(scores.reduce(cute.ReductionOp.ADD, Float32.zero, 0))
    cute.gemm(pv_atom, out, scores, v, out)
    cute.copy(store_atom, out, gmem_out)
    ctx = fi_e(ctx, EV_ATTENTION, aux)
    ctx = fi_close(ctx)
    return ctx, pack_record(EV_ATTENTION, aux), META

event_boundaries.end: After the final attention output and store completion are visible.

import os
from cutlass import Float16, Float32, Int32, Int64, cute
from fi_cute import fi_open, fi_b, fi_e, fi_close

EV_SOFTMAX = Int32(16)
ARCH = os.environ["WEAVEPROFILER_ARCH"]  # sm_90, sm_100a, or sm_103a
BACKEND = "cutedsl_nv"
GRAN = 0  # 0=warp lane 0; 1=linear CTA thread 0
META = {"arch": ARCH, "backend": BACKEND, "gran": "warp" if GRAN == 0 else "cta"}

@cute.jit
def pack_record(tag: Int32, aux: Int32) -> Int64:
    return (Int64(aux) << 32) | (Int64(tag) & Int64(0xFFFFFFFF))

@cute.jit
def softmax_segment(records, overflow, fragment):
    ctx = fi_open(records, overflow, EV_SOFTMAX, Int32(8), fi_level=2, fi_gran=GRAN)
    values = fragment.load().to(Float32)
    aux = Int32(0)
    ctx = fi_b(ctx, EV_SOFTMAX, aux)
    row_max = values.reduce(cute.ReductionOp.MAX, -Float32.inf, 0)
    numerator = cute.math.exp2(values - row_max, fastmath=True)
    denominator = numerator.reduce(cute.ReductionOp.ADD, Float32.zero, 0)
    probabilities = numerator * cute.arch.rcp_approx(denominator)
    ctx = fi_e(ctx, EV_SOFTMAX, aux)
    fragment.store(probabilities)
    ctx = fi_close(ctx)
    return ctx, pack_record(EV_SOFTMAX, aux), META

event_boundaries.end: After normalized probabilities are materialized and visible to the consumer.

ARCH = os.environ["WEAVEPROFILER_ARCH"]  # sm_90, sm_100a, or sm_103a

def pack_record(tag: Int32, aux: Int32) -> Int64:

def reduction_segment(records, overflow, fragment):
    ctx = fi_open(records, overflow, EV_REDUCTION, Int32(8), fi_level=2, fi_gran=GRAN)

import os
from cutlass import Float16, Float32, Int32, Int64, cute
from fi_cute import fi_open, fi_b, fi_e, fi_close

EV_LOAD = Int32(1)
ARCH = os.environ["WEAVEPROFILER_ARCH"]  # sm_90, sm_100a, or sm_103a
BACKEND = "cutedsl_nv"
GRAN = 0  # 0=warp lane 0; 1=linear CTA thread 0
META = {"arch": ARCH, "backend": BACKEND, "gran": "warp" if GRAN == 0 else "cta"}

@cute.jit
def pack_record(tag: Int32, aux: Int32) -> Int64:
    return (Int64(aux) << 32) | (Int64(tag) & Int64(0xFFFFFFFF))

@cute.jit
def load_segment(records, overflow, tiled_copy, gmem_src, smem_dst, barrier_ptr):
    ctx = fi_open(records, overflow, EV_LOAD, Int32(8), fi_level=2, fi_gran=GRAN)
    aux = Int32(0)
    ctx = fi_b(ctx, EV_LOAD, aux)
    cute.copy(tiled_copy, gmem_src, smem_dst, tma_bar_ptr=barrier_ptr)
    cute.arch.cp_async_commit_group()
    cute.arch.cp_async_wait_group(0)
    ctx = fi_e(ctx, EV_LOAD, aux)
    ctx = fi_close(ctx)
    return ctx, pack_record(EV_LOAD, aux), META

def compute_segment(records, overflow, fragment, scale, bias):

import os

from fi_cute import fi_open, fi_b, fi_e, fi_close

EV_COMMUNICATION = Int32(9)
ARCH = os.environ["WEAVEPROFILER_ARCH"]  # sm_90, sm_100a, or sm_103a
BACKEND = "cutedsl_nv"
GRAN = 0  # 0=warp lane 0; 1=linear CTA thread 0
META = {"arch": ARCH, "backend": BACKEND, "gran": "warp" if GRAN == 0 else "cta"}

@cute.jit
def pack_record(tag: Int32, aux: Int32) -> Int64:
    return (Int64(aux) << 32) | (Int64(tag) & Int64(0xFFFFFFFF))

@cute.jit
def communication_segment(records, overflow, value, peer_value, peer_ready, rank, num_ranks):
    ctx = fi_open(records, overflow, EV_COMMUNICATION, Int32(8), fi_level=2, fi_gran=GRAN)
    aux = rank
    ctx = fi_b(ctx, EV_COMMUNICATION, aux)
    local = value[rank]
    peer_value[rank] = local
    cute.arch.atomic_add(peer_ready.iterator, Int32(1))
    total = Float32.zero
    for peer in range(num_ranks):
        while peer_ready[peer] < Int32(num_ranks):
            pass
        total = total + peer_value[peer]
    value[rank] = total
    ctx = fi_e(ctx, EV_COMMUNICATION, aux)
    ctx = fi_close(ctx)
    return ctx, pack_record(EV_COMMUNICATION, aux), META
